title: What Pervasive Game Platforms Is
definition: Pervasive Game Platforms: platforms for always-on pervasive games.
description:
Pervasive Game Platforms is platforms for always-on pervasive games. It sits squarely in Future Entertainment & Play, the frontier where ambient engines science becomes platform logistics infrastructure.

The stakes are opt-outs-scale. Societies that master platform hulls early will shape consent design practice for generations; societies that wait will buy it from those who did not. That is why ambient engines programs worldwide now treat Pervasive Game Platforms as a strategic capability, not a curiosity.

Inside this database: the concept defined precisely, today's real research landscape, the six component pieces every Pervasive Game Platforms needs, five dated milestones, three runnable simulators, practice drills, the key organizations, and a master roadmap — each record with its own demo program.

title: Real Research Today: Pervasive Game Platforms
definition: Today's documented research behind Pervasive Game Platforms.
description:
The road to Pervasive Game Platforms is already being paved. Location-based VR (Sandbox VR, Zero Latency) scales shared immersive play. The global games industry ($180B+) out-earns film and music combined.

The Olympic Esports Series and IOC Esports Commission legitimize competitive gaming. Together these programs form the ambient engines foundation that Pervasive Game Platforms will build on — the platform logistics results, the consent design methods, and the institutional memory.

Forecasts are projections, not promises: the dated milestones in this database reflect published roadmaps and expert surveys, and they will move as platform logistics research advances. Treat every date as a planning scenario with error bars, and watch the signals listed in each milestone record.

title: Readiness Estimator: Pervasive Game Platforms
definition: Estimates Pervasive Game Platforms readiness from component maturity.
description:
The estimator scores the six Pervasive Game Platforms components on the TRL 1–9 scale and averages them into a verdict: research phase, pilot phase, or deployment phase. Scores derive from the component records in this database — change a component's maturity and the verdict moves.

Honest scoring is the point: a platform hulls that averages TRL 3 is not failing, it is three phases from deployment, and the estimator tells you which component drags the average down. Fund that one first.

title: Pervasive Game Platforms Systems Simulator
definition: Simulates Pervasive Game Platforms operating for a day.
description:
The simulator walks a Pervasive Game Platforms installation through six operating steps, with seeded randomness standing in for real-world variation. Seed 47901 reproduces this exact run — change the seed in the program to explore other days.

Watch for DEGRADED steps: they mark where ambient engines monitoring, platform logistics redundancy, or consent design maintenance would intervene in a real deployment. A simulator that never degrades is lying; this one degrades about eight percent of the time, like early hardware does.

title: Pervasive Game Platforms Master Roadmap
definition: The united roadmap for Pervasive Game Platforms: prove, build, operate, compound.
description:
The master roadmap for Pervasive Game Platforms — platforms for always-on pervasive games.

Phase 1 — Prove (ambient engines): laboratory demonstrations of every component, replicated independently. No scaling until the physics is boring.

Phase 2 — Build (platform logistics): pilot manufacturing and integration. The six pieces meet for the first time and the interfaces get honest.

Phase 3 — Operate (consent design): continuous real-world operation. Uptime, cost curves and failure data replace projections.

Phase 4 — Compound (opt-outs): platform hulls as everyday infrastructure. Costs collapse, standards settle, and players-scale deployment begins.

Public edition: phases follow documented research readiness. This record unites the database: overview, research, components, milestones, demos and drills all point here.

Each phase has exit criteria.
